title: Browser Use vs Hyperbrowser: Pricing, Stealth & Features
summary: Compare Browser Use vs Hyperbrowser on pricing, stealth, performance, and session management. Find the right platform for your browser automation workflows.
body_markdown:
Choosing a cloud browser also means choosing how you'll pay for it and which parts of your workflow the platform will handle. Browser Use combines managed browser infrastructure with hosted agents, while Hyperbrowser bundles browsers and agents with web-data APIs and code sandboxes.


Below, we'll look at the cost of running the same workload, access to protected sites, and the session controls that matter when connecting your own scripts.


## TL;DR


Choose Browser Use for subscription-free browser infrastructure with lower published browser and managed-proxy rates, plus its own hosted agents. Consider Hyperbrowser when you specifically need Fetch, Crawl, and Search endpoints alongside your browsers.


Compare Browser Use Hyperbrowser


Primary offering Browser infrastructure and hosted agents Browser infrastructure, hosted agents, and web-data APIs


Pricing model Pay as you go Usage-based credits


Free plan $1 signup credit (one-time) 5,000 free credits ($5)


Browser time $0.06/hour, rounded up to whole minutes $0.10/hour


Managed proxy traffic $5/GB $10/GB; paid plan required


Concurrency Starts at 10; up to 1,000 based on spend Free: 1; Startup: 25; Scale: 100


Stealth Enabled by default Standard mode; Ultra on Enterprise


CDP disconnect Runs until stopped or timed out Stops by default; keep-alive optional


Compliance SOC 2 Type II, DPA; HIPAA support and zero data retention on Enterprise SOC 2 Type I


∗ Pricing checked November 24, 2026; rates exclude agent inference.
∗ Concurrency scales with qualifying Browser Use payments; enterprise limits vary.
∗ Other capabilities checked November 17, 2026; benchmark limitations appear below.
∗ Compliance:[Browser Use](https://browser-use.com/security) and[Hyperbrowser](https://trust.hyperbrowser.ai/) , checked November 24, 2026.


## What Is Browser Use?


Browser Use offers two cloud products:


- [Browser Infrastructure](https://browser-use.com/stealth-browsers) provides managed Chromium browsers for your scripts and agents. Connect through the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) using Playwright or Puppeteer.
- [Browser Use Agents](https://browser-use.com/web-agents) accepts a task, operates the browser, and returns the result. The service manages the agent loop.


The open-source` browser-use` library lets you run and customize an agent yourself. Using Browser Use Infrastructure doesn't require that library or rewriting your existing scripts as natural-language tasks.


## What Is Hyperbrowser?


[Hyperbrowser](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/quickstart) provides managed browsers that you can control through its API and existing automation tools. It also offers hosted agents, including HyperAgent and integrations with other agent frameworks.


Its[Web API](https://hyperbrowser.ai/docs/web/overview) provides Fetch, Crawl, and Search endpoints for collecting web content. These sit alongside the browser sessions, so an application can use a dedicated data endpoint for one operation and browser automation for another.


It also offers code sandboxes billed from the same credit balance, useful when your application needs compute alongside browser automation.


Hyperbrowser also[hosts the open-source Browser Use agent](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/agents/browser-use) . In that setup, Hyperbrowser runs the library on its infrastructure. It's a separate service from Browser Use Cloud, with its own supported versions, models, and billing.


## Comparison


The browser infrastructure overlaps directly. Let's start there, then look at the agent and API differences that affect how you build a workflow.


### Pricing


[Browser Use pricing](https://browser-use.com/pricing) is usage-based: $0.06 per browser-hour, rounded up to whole minutes, plus $5/GB for managed residential proxy traffic. No subscription is required, and purchased credits don't expire.


Direct traffic costs $0.20/GB. The same network rate applies when using your own proxy, with the external proxy bill separate;[custom proxies require enterprise access for new projects](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/billing) .


[Hyperbrowser pricing](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/pricing) starts with 5,000 free credits, worth $5. Startup costs $30/month and includes $30 in usage; Scale costs $100/month and includes $100. Browser time consumes $0.10/hour, while managed proxy traffic consumes $10/GB.


Those free credits let you try browser sessions, but[proxies](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/sessions/proxy) and[CAPTCHA solving](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/sessions/captcha-solving) require a paid plan. If your target sites need either, budget for at least Startup.


Hyperbrowser's[subscription credits refresh each billing period](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/pricing) and don't roll over. Additional purchased credits expire after 12 months. The credit pool can also pay for agents and web-data requests.


Suppose your monthly workload uses 100 billable browser-hours and 2 GB of managed proxy traffic, within Startup's concurrency limit:


Cost component Browser Use Hyperbrowser Startup


Browser time $6 $10 in credits


Proxy traffic $10 $20 in credits


Monthly cost $16 in usage $30 subscription, covering all $30 of usage


Browser Use costs less for this example. Hyperbrowser's subscription already includes the consumed credits, so there's no additional $30 usage charge. This is an illustrative bill, assuming equal billable usage and excluding inference, promotions, taxes, and other services.


Agent costs need a separate comparison. Browser Use's[supported bring-your-own-key (BYOK) path](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/billing#what-does-byok-pay-for) bills model usage through your provider and adds a 20% orchestration fee, plus browser/network charges.


Hyperbrowser[lists $0.02 per step](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/pricing#ai-agents) for HyperAgent and its hosted Browser Use integration, plus browser and proxy usage. The latter's[BYOK option](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/agents/browser-use#use-your-own-api-keys) removes the step charge; your model provider still bills inference. Comparing agent costs requires the same task and configuration.


### Stealth


Browser Use runs a[hardened Chromium fork](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/stealth) with stealth enabled by default. Hyperbrowser provides standard stealth mode, proxies, and CAPTCHA solving, with[Ultra Stealth reserved for Enterprise](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/sessions/stealth) .


In[Stealth Bench V2](https://browser-use.com/benchmarks/browsers) , measured September 25, 2026, Browser Use reached usable content on 90.5% of visits, versus Hyperbrowser's 73.5%. A model judged page evidence from two visits per provider to each of 100 protected sites, with 60 seconds allowed per visit.


Two Hyperbrowser visits were[unresolved](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark/tree/74b427184d84b0df391a9c337def5aadf115a893/stealth_bench/official_results) ; counting both as successful would raise its result to 74.5%. Browser Use had no unresolved visits.


Browser Use published the study and chose sites where it had previously succeeded while stock Chromium with a US proxy failed, favoring Browser Use. Hyperbrowser used standard stealth, its managed proxy, and native solver; Ultra wasn't tested. These results measure access to that selected set of sites, not completed logins, forms, or agent tasks.


### Performance & Limits


[ComputeSDK's November 13 lifecycle benchmark](https://www.computesdk.com/benchmarks/browsers/compare/browseruse-vs-hyperbrowser) creates a session, connects Playwright over CDP, loads` example.com` , and releases the session.


Result Browser Use Hyperbrowser


Successful runs 100/100 100/100


Median complete lifecycle 370 ms 704 ms


These medians cover the complete lifecycle. The[benchmark used different runners](https://github.com/computesdk/benchmarks/blob/82ad5c858105a83178ca354621b2a2159d1aeea9/.github/workflows/browser-benchmarks.yml) : AWS us-east-2 for Browser Use and Namespace for Hyperbrowser. Runner and network differences affect latency, so the figures don't establish a same-location speed advantage or faster agent tasks.


Capacity differs too. Browser Use starts at[10 concurrent sessions](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/concurrency) ; $100 in qualifying project payments unlocks 50. That payment remains usable credit. Hyperbrowser's plans provide one concurrent session on Free, 25 on Startup, and 100 on Scale.


Browser Use's[browser API caps sessions at four hours](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/api-v4/browsers/create-browser-session) . Hyperbrowser's[creation schema](https://hyperbrowser.ai/docs/api-reference/create-new-session) accepts timeouts up to 720 minutes, but that parameter bound doesn't establish the allowance on every plan. Check the applicable team limit before choosing it for a long-running workflow.


### Developer Experience & Sessions


Both support Playwright and Puppeteer, so existing automation code can use either provider's remote browser. Hyperbrowser also offers[Selenium access](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/sessions/selenium) on request. Browser Use's[connection guide](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/playwright-puppeteer-selenium) directs remote WebSocket connections to Playwright or Puppeteer because Selenium's` debugger_address` expects a local host and port.


For debugging,[Browser Use](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/live-preview) and[Hyperbrowser](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/sessions/recordings) both offer session recordings. Hyperbrowser's rrweb recordings capture DOM changes, interactions, and network requests; it also offers MP4 video. Use a live view to inspect an active run and a recording to retrace where a failed workflow went wrong.


Session cleanup is a practical difference. With[Browser Use](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) , closing the CDP connection leaves the managed browser running; explicitly stop it to end runtime billing.[Hyperbrowser](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/sessions/lifecycle) normally stops the session on CDP disconnect. Add` keepAlive=true` to its CDP URL to reconnect later, but keep at least one page open; closing every page still stops the session.


Both support saved logins. Browser Use can[sync local cookies](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/profile-sync) , while Hyperbrowser lets you[attach a persistent profile](https://www.hyperbrowser.ai/docs/sessions/profiles) and save changes for later sessions. A profile preserves browser state between sessions; it doesn't keep an open page running.


Browser Use's hosted agents support a[1Password integration](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/guides/1password) . Hyperbrowser's[credential-fill preview](https://hyperbrowser.ai/docs/sessions/credentials) supports stored secrets, one-time codes, and 1Password, with access enabled on request. Neither removes the possibility of a login requiring human approval.


## Conclusion


For existing Playwright or Puppeteer scripts, Browser Use is a good starting point when browser and proxy costs drive your choice. The example above costs $16 versus $30 on Hyperbrowser Startup, and you can buy credits without committing to a monthly plan.


Hyperbrowser is worth considering when the same application needs Fetch, Crawl, Search, or code sandboxes alongside browsers. Its shared credit pool can cover those services too. For Selenium workloads, confirm access with its team before choosing it.


For hosted agents, test the same task on both and compare completed results, total cost, and failures that need intervention. Lower browser rates and stronger access scores alone don't tell you which agent will finish your workflow more reliably.


To try your existing scripts on Browser Use, start with the[connection guide](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/playwright-puppeteer-selenium) .
